definitions.gloss: second half; second half of a fiscal year; latter half of a business period
definitions.explanation: The second half of a fiscal year or accounting period. In Japan, where the fiscal year typically runs April to March, the second half is October to March.

examples.japanese: {下期|しもき}の{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てる。
examples.english: To make plans for the second half.

examples.japanese: {下期|しもき}から{新|あたら}しいプロジェクトが{始|はじ}まる。
examples.english: A new project starts in the second half.

examples.japanese: {上期|かみき}は{赤字|あかじ}だったが、{下期|しもき}で{巻|ま}き{返|かえ}して{通期|つうき}では{黒字|くろじ}になった。
examples.english: The first half was in the red, but they recovered in the second half and ended the full year in the black.

notes:
A business and financial term referring to the second half of a fiscal year. In Japan's standard fiscal year (April–March), {下期|しもき} covers October–March.

PRONUNCIATION:
Also read as かき in some contexts, though しもき is the more common pronunciation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下期|しもき}{決算|けっさん}: second-half financial results
- {下期|しもき}{見通|みとお}し: second-half outlook
- {下期|しもき}{予算|よさん}: second-half budget
- {下期|しもき}{業績|ぎょうせき}: second-half performance

RELATED WORDS:
- {上期|かみき}: first half (of fiscal year)
- {通期|つうき}: full year
- {半期|はんき}: half period
- {四半期|しはんき}: quarter

DOMAIN:
Used in corporate reports, earnings announcements, and business planning. Rarely appears outside financial and business contexts.
